$comment: Plan 8.3: prompts and normalization rules are frozen before the held-out collection is processed for the first time. This file is that freeze, and evaluation/src/freeze.test.ts enforces it: change any constant below without changing this file and the suite fails. Editing a value here to make the test pass is not a fix, it is a new freeze, and it invalidates the generalization claim unless the held-out set is rerun. Re-frozen once: NORMALIZATION_VERSION moved to normalize@2 when generic subjects ("document", "this presentation") were scoped to their own document, after merging them across files produced a false contradiction between two filing dates. The generalization run under normalize@1 was throttled and produced no measured accuracy, so nothing measured is invalidated by this; a future generalization claim must be made under normalize@2. Re-frozen again: EXTRACTION_PROMPT_VERSION moved to claim-extract@2 when the collection's predicate registry began being shown to extraction, after measurement found 1,053 distinct predicates across 1,991 claims and only two (entity, predicate) pairs shared between documents — leaving cross-document retrieval nothing to match on. Re-frozen a third time: CHECKS_VERSION moved to checks@2 when a context dimension stopped counting as different where only one document stated it. corroborates requires zero context differences, so treating silence as disagreement had blocked every deterministic corroboration in the collection. Re-frozen a fourth time: CHECKS_VERSION moved to checks@3 when the checks began reporting contextConfirmed — whether the two contexts are known to match, as against merely not known to differ — and the deterministic corroboration rule began requiring it, along with a resolved entity match on both sides. checks@2 had made silence stop counting as disagreement, which was right, but left an empty difference list meaning both agreement and silence; two claims stating no period at all could therefore corroborate each other. The same rule now runs before classification rather than only in the classifier's absence, so a pair with no open question costs no call. Nothing about which pairs may be contradicted or reconciled changed: those still go to the model. Re-frozen a fifth time: EXTRACTION_PROMPT_VERSION moved to claim-extract@3 when extraction began packing several small chunks into one request. Chunking still flushes at every heading and page, so the chunks and their citations are unchanged; what changed is that a request may now carry several of them as separate passages, under a system prompt written in the plural and with block handles made unique across the batch. A request carrying one passage is asked exactly what claim-extract@2 asked, so a document whose chunks do not pack is unaffected in substance — but the version has to move, because whether a chunk was asked alone or beside others is now part of what produced its claims.
